Phase 3 · Assessment reference

Assessment & Submission

The final committee decision is evaluated as both an auditable technical package and a persuasive oral defense.

Canvas is the submission authority

Canvas remains the authority for due dates, submission mechanics, and course-grade weights. Use the Investment Project Submission rubric for the written decision package and the Investment Project Presentation rubric for the live committee presentation and defense.

Investment Project Submission rubric · 100 points

Written decision package

CriterionWeightCommittee-ready standard
Evidence quality & technical accuracy20%Claims, calculations, formulas, sources, FactSet retrieval records, as-of dates, and portfolio metrics are correct, comparable, traceable, and interpreted; required licensed evidence is submitted privately through Canvas and AI output is never treated as evidence.
Focused security selection20%Each client portfolio contains 8–10 holdings and never more than 10; funds and ETFs are primary, individual securities total no more than two or three, final holdings have concise scorecards, and realistic alternatives are rejected briefly without duplicate exposure or unnecessary concentration.
Client suitability & IPS compliance15%Each recommendation traces to Phase 1 client needs and guardrails, and the IPS scorecard tests all relevant objectives and RRTTLLU constraints.
Shared portfolio quality & risk response25%Final selection and weights, diversification, overlap, concentration, portfolio trade-offs, stress results, breaches, corrective trades, re-tests, and the supported hedge or no-hedge conclusion form one internally consistent portfolio decision.
Individual role evidence & decision trail20%For each student, role-specific evidence is identifiable and peer-reviewed, and the Analyst Decision Log records recommendation(s), alternative(s) rejected, a key trade-off, contribution to integration or residual-risk decisions, and the link to the committee vote.

Investment Project Presentation rubric · 100 points

Live committee presentation and defense

The defense is part of the presentation

Keep the existing final presentation and include a compact investment-committee defense within it. Each student must be ready for targeted questions tied to role-specific evidence, the Analyst Decision Log contribution, an alternative rejected, a key trade-off, and the integrated portfolio decision.

CriterionWeightCommittee-ready standard
Role-specific committee defense25%Within the presentation's compact investment-committee defense, each member answers targeted questions for their role, uses relevant evidence and calculations, acknowledges uncertainty, and defends or revises the judgment under challenge.
Individual evidence & Decision Log contribution20%Each member demonstrates command of owned evidence and can explain their recommendation, alternative rejected, key trade-off, Decision Log contribution, verification, and limitations.
Shared portfolio quality & integration25%The committee presents one coherent chain from client discovery through the focused 8–10 holding selection, final weights, overlap/concentration decisions, stress results, hedge or no-hedge conclusion, correction, and final recommendation.
Client suitability & risk compliance20%Members can show where client needs changed the portfolio, explain the strongest bear case and residual risk, and defend compliance, corrective action, and the hedge or no-hedge conclusion.
Clarity, professionalism & visual evidence10%The team communicates concisely as client-focused professionals and uses legible exhibits that make the recommendation, trade-offs, and evidence visible.

Live defense question bank

Prepare to defend owned work and the integrated decision

The panel may direct any question to any member. Role ownership determines preparation responsibility, not permission to ignore the rest of the portfolio.

Client and Macro Strategist

  • Which Phase 1 client fact or guardrail most changed the final portfolio, and where can the committee see that change?
  • Which macro assumption matters most to this recommendation, and what evidence would cause the team to revise it?
  • Which unresolved client information gap remains material, and how did the portfolio avoid pretending it was known?

Fixed-Income Analyst

  • Why does the selected fixed-income exposure fit the client's cash-flow horizon better than the strongest alternative?
  • What happens to price and income if rates or credit spreads move against the position, and which duration or credit evidence supports that answer?
  • What did the Holding & Exposure Reality Check reveal about concentration, liquidity, costs, key risk, and the allocation implication for the selected fixed-income exposure?

Equity Analyst

  • Why does the selected equity fund or ETF deliver the needed exposure better than the strongest alternative after costs, liquidity, overlap, and style or sector concentration?
  • If the portfolio includes an individual equity, why is it superior to a fund or ETF for that role, what is its idiosyncratic risk, and why is the position size appropriate?
  • Which equity candidate did you reject, and what key trade-off separated it from your recommendation?

Portfolio Manager

  • Which analyst recommendations did you integrate, resize, or reject, and what explicit portfolio trade-off drove each decision?
  • Where did you resolve overlap or concentration, and why are the final 8–10 holdings and weights better than the strongest alternative mix?
  • If the committee rejects one proposed adjustment, what alternative preserves the client goal and what new trade-off does it create?

Risk and Derivatives Analyst

  • Which residual risk contributes most to the bear-case loss, and which client goal is therefore most exposed?
  • Why is the supported conclusion hedge or no hedge, and what evidence makes that conclusion preferable to changing the underlying holdings or weights?
  • If a hedge is proposed, explain the instrument, size, cost, liquidity, trade-offs, residual risk, and adjustment or removal condition.

Any committee member

  • What was the team's strongest initial judgment that changed after AI challenge and human verification?
  • Which FactSet retrieval most affected the recommendation, how did you interpret it, and where is the licensed-source evidence retained under course policy?
  • Which source or calculation carries the most decision weight, and what are its limitations?
  • What is the strongest reasonable case against the final recommendation?
  • What monitoring trigger would force the committee to reconvene before the normal review date?

Final readiness check

Before the committee meeting

  • Executive recommendation and decision memo
  • Technical exhibit book linking macro, mandate, allocation, securities, and risk
  • Client-specific recommendation for all three assigned clients
  • Final decision record with vote, reservations, and implementation actions
  • Visual oral presentation with balanced speaking time and a compact investment-committee defense
  • Role-specific evidence and targeted-question preparation for all five seats
  • Cross-functional Q&A preparation

Q&A standard

Every member must be able to defend the market view, mandate, allocation, security choices, stress test, and trade-offs. The panel may direct a question to a member who did not lead that workstream.
